deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is one of a series of index tables for the Gaussian prime moduli -5+6i (norm 61), 7+2i (norm 53) and 9+4i (norm 97). They serve Gauss's work on biquadratic (quartic) residues.

(A) Main table, modulus pi = 7+2i, N(pi) = 53, (Z[i]/pi)* cyclic of order 52.
- Column 3 lists r_k = (1+i)^k, reduced to an absolutely least residue:
  1, 1+i, 2i, -2+2i, 3+2i, 3-2i, -2-i, -1-3i, 3i, -1-4i, 1+2i, -1+3i, -4+2i, and then 1 again at k = 13.
  So (1+i)^13 = 1 (mod pi), and 1+i has order 13.
- Column 2 is the reduction device. It holds r_k*(7-2i) with both coordinates reduced mod 53 = (7+2i)(7-2i):
  7-2i, 9+5i, 4+14i, -10+18i, 25+8i, 17-20i, -16-3i, -13-19i, 6+21i, -15-26i, 11+12i, -1+23i, -24+22i, 7-2i.
  Recursion: multiply the previous entry by 1+i and reduce each coordinate mod 53. For example (-10+18i)(1+i) = -28+8i, which reduces to 25+8i.
  Then r = (entry)*(7+2i)/53.
  This works because x = y (mod pi) iff x*conj(pi) = y*conj(pi) (mod 53).
- Column 5 is i*r_k: -1+i, -2, -2-2i, -2+3i, 2+3i, 1-2i, 3-i, -3, 4-i, -2+i, -3-i, -2-4i, i.
- The number columns are indices relative to the primitive root g = -1+i = i(1+i).
  - ind(i*(1+i)^k) = 1, 41, 29, 17, 5, 45, 33, 21, 9, 49, 37, 25, 13.
  - ind((1+i)^k) = 40k mod 52 = 40, 28, 16, 4, 44, 32, 20, 8, 48, 36, 24, 12.
  - ind(i) = 13, i.e. g^13 = i.
  - Hence for any z, z^13 = z^((N-1)/4) = i^(ind z): the index mod 4 gives the quartic character [z/pi]_4 directly.
  - Also ind(1+i) = 40 = 0 mod 4, so 1+i is a biquadratic residue of 7+2i. This agrees with the supplementary law, since (a-b-b^2-1)/4 = 0 for a=7, b=2.

(B) Reducing the other small primary primes mod 7+2i.
- Top block: z*(7-2i) = (7a+2b) + (7b-2a)i, computed for z = -5+2i, -1+6i, 5+4i, 7+2i, -5+6i, -3+8i. These are the moduli of the neighbouring tables.
- Side column: the reduced products mod 53, z*(7-2i) for z = -5+-2i, -1+-6i, 5+-4i, 7-2i, -5+-6i, -3+-8i:
  22+24i, 14-4i, 5-9i, -19+13i, -10+18i, -26+15i, -8+25i, -23-i, 6+21i, -5+9i, 16+3i.
  From the -8 entry on, the imaginary parts are written one line lower.
- Middle block: 7A and -2B (rows 1-2), 7B and 2A (rows 3-4). Then (A+Bi)(7+2i)/53 = ((7A-2B) + (2A+7B)i)/53, giving the residues:
  -5+2i = 2+4i, -5-2i = 2, -1+6i = 1-i, -1-6i = -3+i, 5+4i = -2+2i, 5-4i = -4+i, 7-2i = -2+3i, -5+6i = -3-i, -5-6i = 3i, -3+8i = -1+i, -3-8i = 2+i.
- Same procedure, residue in the last line:
  - 1-4i = -1+3i
  - -7 = 2i
  - 5+8i = -i
  - 5-8i = 3-i
  - 9+4i = 2+2i
  - 9-4i = i
  - -1+10i = 1+3i (via 13+19i)
  - -1-10i = 4-i
  - 3-10i = 1-3i
  - 3+10i = -2+i
  - -7+8i = 2+3i
  - -7-8i = -2+i
- Products only, which can be looked up in column 2 or as i times an entry:
  - -11 gives -24+22i, so -11 = -4+2i.
  - -11+4i gives -16-3i (= -2-i).
  - -11-4i gives 21-6i (= 3; my lookup).
  - 7+10i gives 16+3i (= 2+i).
  - 7-10i gives -24+22i, after an erased first attempt (= -4+2i).
  - 11+6i gives -17+20i.
  - 11-6i gives 12-11i.
  - -13+2i gives 19-13i.
  - -13-2i gives 11+12i.
  - -9+10i gives 10-18i.
  - -9-10i gives 23+i.
  - -7+12i gives -25-8i.
  - -7-12i gives -20-17i.
- All these z are primary in Gauss's sense: b even, a+b = 1 mod 4. Their norms run through 29, ..., 193 and also include 121 (from -11) and 49 (from -7).
- So the page tabulates the biquadratic characters of the primary primes with respect to 7+2i. These are raw data for testing biquadratic reciprocity.

(C) Bottom.
- (1-i)*i = 1+i.
- Modulus -3+8i (norm 73): (-1+6i)(-3-8i) = 51-10i, which reduces to -22-10i. Then (-22-10i)(-3+8i) = 146-146i = 73(2-2i).
  So -1+6i = 2-2i = (1+i)(1-i)^2 (mod -3+8i).
- '(1-i)^9 = -i', '(-1)^9 = -1': most plausibly ((1-i)^2)^9 = (-2i)^9 = -2^9 i = -i, since 2^9 = 512 = 1 mod 73. This is (1-i)^18 = (1-i)^((73-1)/4), the quartic character of 1-i. My reading of the shorthand.
  Consistently, (2-2i)^18 = -i (mod -3+8i), so [-1+6i / -3+8i]_4 = -i.
errors: Middle block, entry for -8+25i (the image of 7-2i): the -2B row shows -30 where -2*25 = -50 is required. The quotient Gauss records (-56-50)/53 = -2 is correct, so this is a slip or misreading only.
As literally written, '(1-i)^9 = -i' is false modulo -3+8i: (1-i)^9 = 16-16i = 2-3i there. The true statement is (1-i)^18 = ((1-i)^2)^9 = -i. Probably shorthand rather than an error.
No other arithmetic errors found. Every power, product and reduction I checked (all rows of the table, all side products, all quotients) is correct.

results.what: Index table modulo the Gaussian prime 7+2i with primitive root -1+i. (1+i) has order 13, i has index 13, and residues are computed via multiplication by the conjugate 7-2i and coordinatewise reduction mod 53.
results.modern_name: Discrete logarithm (index) table in Z[i]/(pi); reduction via pi*conj(pi) = p
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Gaussian integers, Theoria residuorum biquadraticorum 1828/1832); index tables go back to Gauss/Jacobi (Canon arithmeticus 1839)

results.what: Tabulation of residues and quartic characters of the primary primes of norm up to about 193 (and -7, -11) modulo 7+2i, as data for biquadratic reciprocity
results.modern_name: Quartic residue symbol computations / numerical verification of biquadratic reciprocity
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (law stated 1832, unproved); first published proofs Jacobi (lectures 1836-37) and Eisenstein (1844)

results.what: 1+i is a biquadratic residue of 7+2i (index 40 = 0 mod 4)
results.modern_name: Supplementary law of biquadratic reciprocity for 1+i

results.what: Quartic character of -1+6i modulo -3+8i via -1+6i = (1+i)(1-i)^2 and (1-i)^18 = -i (mod -3+8i)
results.modern_name: Evaluation of a quartic residue symbol

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine numerical tables of indices and biquadratic characters for small Gaussian primes. They belong to Gauss's well-documented work on biquadratic residues (1820s-1832), whose Nachlass is known to contain such computations. The conjugate-multiplication reduction trick is efficient but elementary.

checkable.asserts: g = -1+i satisfies g^13 = i, so index of i is 13
g^26 = -1, so -1+i is a primitive root mod 7+2i (order 52, given g^4 != 1)
supplementary-law exponent for 1+i mod 7+2i is 0, consistent with index 40 = 0 mod 4
